Consistent research workflows

Source: vignettes/strict-workflows.Rmd
strict-workflows.Rmd

The strict profile fixes the project structure in deterministic templates. The research declaration chooses domain, data origin and study design independently. The same eleven stages remain visible in every project: protocol, import, validation, cleaning, descriptive analysis, primary analysis, diagnostics, sensitivity analysis, exploration, report and reproducibility. An inapplicable stage requires a reason. A stage name does not prescribe a statistical method.

library(reflowR)
## reflowR v0.1.0.9000 — Themed Workflowr Extensions (CTTIR v5)
## Use reflow_init() to get started.
## See reflow_schemes() and reflow_presets() for options.
profile <- reflow_profile("clinical", "secondary", "observational", seed = 104L)
profile[c("domain", "data_origin", "design", "scheme", "primary_color", "badge")]
## $domain
## [1] "clinical"
## 
## $data_origin
## [1] "secondary"
## 
## $design
## [1] "observational"
## 
## $scheme
## [1] "clinical"
## 
## $primary_color
## [1] "#D55E00"
## 
## $badge
## [1] "SECONDARY DATA"

The palette follows the CTTIR v5 families: clinical projects use clinical (vermillion) and basic research uses brand (blue). Methods, simulation and software use methods; evidence synthesis uses evidence. Other domains use platform. Primary or secondary data are shown as a separate text badge, so colour is not the sole indicator of the project category. Declarations recorded with the earlier palette keep their scheme, colour and stylesheet and still validate.

Declare access, jurisdiction and the intended legal basis explicitly. These are recorded statements, not a determination that a project is authorized. Unknown values prevent execution readiness.

profile <- reflow_profile("basic", "primary", "simulation", seed = 104L,
  data_access = "synthetic", jurisdiction = "Germany",
  legal_basis = "Generated teaching data without personal records")
lock <- jsonlite::read_json("reviewed-environment/renv.lock")
scaffold <- reflow_scaffold(profile, "Example study", "Research group", lock)
project <- reflow_init_strict("example-study", profile, "Example study",
  "Research group", lock, git = TRUE)

Initialization writes a new directory and, when requested, initializes an empty Git repository. It does not install dependencies, commit, render or publish. Provision the exact locked R and package versions in a reviewed external R library before execution. This profile does not generate a project-local renv activation script or library. The root lock declares the required environment; stage execution checks installed versions and GitHub revision pins.

Preserve scaffold$declaration outside the project. The project cannot approve its own profile, palette, control files or changed code. Pass externally reviewed SHA-256 hashes for the declared stage files to validation:

reflow_validate_strict("example-study", scaffold$declaration)
reviewed <- c(
  "analysis/05_descriptive.Rmd" = "<reviewed SHA-256>",
  "code/stages/05_descriptive.R" = "<reviewed SHA-256>"
)
reflow_validate_strict("example-study", scaffold$declaration, reviewed)

valid means the structure and supplied hashes agree. execution_ready also requires declarations and reviewed implementations for every applicable stage. completed additionally requires externally retained receipt hashes and matching current code, input and output hashes. Rendering an empty scaffold does not complete an analysis. Receipts record the seed, session and stage outputs; unchanged unrelated artifacts do not count as this stage’s outputs.

Render reviewed pages explicitly with workflowr::wflow_build(). Each build uses workflowr’s fresh R session. Display computed objects explicitly in an Rmd chunk, for example with knitr::kable(summary), after sourcing the calculation helper. Keep raw inputs read-only. Child publications share the root Git repository, dependency lock and site; nested execution roots and unknown code entrypoints fail validation.

Static validation is not a security sandbox, a scientific review or legal approval. Execute reviewed code only within the group’s separately controlled runtime. The existing reflow_init() and preset interfaces remain available for existing projects; adopting the strict profile is an explicit new-project path.

A fixed cttiR composition

strict-cttir-v1 is a separate, opt-in profile. The default strict-v1 declaration and scaffold stay unchanged. The composed profile adds exactly cttir-study.json, cttir-recipe.json and cttir-runtime.json. Each applicable stage calls the fixed installed export cttiR::study_stage(stage = "<declared stage>", directory = "."). The study writer verifies the bound analysis receipt and presents its recorded results. Rendering is not an instruction to recompute the scientific analysis.

profile <- reflow_profile("clinical", "secondary", "observational",
  profile_version = "strict-cttir-v1", data_access = "synthetic",
  jurisdiction = "Germany", legal_basis = "Generated test observations")
composition <- list(
  schema_version = 1L,
  study = reviewed_study,
  recipe = reviewed_recipe,
  runtime = list(package = "cttiR", version = lock$Packages$cttiR$Version,
    writer = "study_stage", files = installed_cttir_file_hashes)
)
scaffold <- reflow_scaffold(profile, "Clinical example", "Research group",
  lock, composition = composition)
project <- reflow_init_strict("clinical-example", profile, "Clinical example",
  "Research group", lock, composition = composition)
reflow_validate_strict(project$directory, scaffold$declaration,
  execution_receipts = external_stage_receipt_hashes)

installed_cttir_file_hashes is a named list of lowercase SHA-256 strings covering every regular file in the reviewed installed cttiR package, including DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, lazy-load databases and package resources. File names are relative to that package directory. Empty or partial inventories, symlinks, unlisted files, changed bytes, a different package version or a missing explicit study_stage export block execution readiness. A clean external R library and session remain required. No package code is loaded by static inventory checking.

The composition itself must be retained in the trusted external declaration. Both scientific objects contain bounded plain JSON values; cttiR, rather than reflowR’s structural validator, validates their study and recipe semantics. All composed stage and control files are immutable: reviewed_files overrides are refused. Changing a study requires a new reviewed declaration and compilation, not a hash waiver for an edited control. No arbitrary extra file list is accepted. The compiled runtime helper also embeds the expected study, recipe, runtime, profile and lock hashes. These identities are checked before writer preflight and again after rendering; replacing a runtime digest map cannot approve changed installed code.

Canonical stage files can be structurally execution-ready when the installed runtime matches and access declarations are complete. They are not completed until current externally pinned execution receipts bind their control, raw input and output hashes. Scientific acceptance, the upstream analysis receipt and its derived-data lineage remain cttiR’s responsibility. These checks do not create an OS sandbox or replace methodological review.
